paper.title: Data-Dependent Regret Bounds for Constrained MABs

settings.name_in_paper: Constrained MAB with adversarial losses and stochastic constraints, soft constraints
unmapped: m stochastic linear constraints with costs in [0,1] drawn i.i.d. from unknown distributions, observed under bandit feedback; thresholds alpha_i known
soft constraints: cumulative positive constraint violation V_T must be sublinear
comparator is the best fixed randomized strategy satisfying the constraints in expectation
learning rate tuning uses knowledge of sum_t l_t^T x* (comparator's cumulative loss)
settings.definition_quote: we focus on constrained MAB problems in which the losses are chosen adversarially and the constraint costs are selected stochastically. ... the loss vector \lvec_t is chosen by an adaptive adversary ... while each cost vector \gvec_{t,i} ... is sampled independently from a probability distribution \mathcal{G}_i. ... V_T := max_i sum_t [g_i^T x_t - alpha_i]^+

settings.name_in_paper: Constrained MAB with adversarial losses and stochastic constraints, hard constraints
unmapped: m stochastic linear constraints with costs in [0,1]; constraints must hold at every round w.h.p.
Slater's condition; learner knows the max-margin strictly feasible strategy x^diamond, its costs theta_i and margin rho
comparator is the best fixed randomized strategy satisfying the constraints in expectation
learning rate tuning uses knowledge of sum_t l_t^T x*
settings.definition_quote: In this setting, the goal of the learner is to guarantee that \gvec_i^\top \xvec_t \leq \alpha_i for every constraint i \in [m] and round t \in [T] with high probability. ... Assumption 2: The learner knows a strictly feasible strategy x^diamond ... and its associated cost theta_i ... rho := min_i [alpha_i - theta_i].

settings.name_in_paper: Constrained MAB with hard constraints (lower bound)
unmapped: stochastic constraints that must hold at every round w.h.p.; strictly feasible strategy with margin rho
loss sequences restricted to the constrained small-loss ball B_{omega,Delta,T}
settings.definition_quote: We define the constrained small-loss balls as B_{omega,Delta,T} := { l_{1:T} in [0,1]^{KT} : sum_t l_t^T x*/T <= omega and sum_t (l_t^T(x^diamond - x*))^2/T <= Delta^2 }.

source.label: thm:viol
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$. Then, with probability at least $1-2\delta$, the \algnamesoft algorithm suffers cumulative positive constraint violations $V_T \le \mathcal{O}\left( \sqrt{KT\ln\left(\nicefrac{TKm}{\delta}\right)} \right).$

results.notes: Bound on cumulative positive constraint violation V_T, not regret. Holds w.p. >= 1-2delta.

symbols.L_xstar: cumulative loss sum_t l_t^T x* of the optimal constrained (randomized) strategy x*

tuning: eta = min{1/(40 H ln T ln(H/delta)), sqrt(K/(L_xstar ln(1/delta)))}, H = ln(ceil(ln T) ceil(3 ln T)/delta)

source.label: thm:reg_soft

results.notes: Comparator is best fixed randomized strategy satisfying constraints in expectation (not necessarily a vertex). Regret defined with l_t^T x_t (expected over action draw). Holds w.p. >= 1-4delta.

symbols.rho: Slater margin of the known strictly feasible strategy x^diamond
symbols.L_xstar: cumulative loss sum_t l_t^T x* of the optimal constrained strategy

conditions: Slater's condition; x^diamond and theta_i known (Assumptions 1-2)
tuning: eta = min{rho/(40 H ln T ln(H/delta)), sqrt(K/(L_xstar ln(1/delta)))}, H = ln(ceil(ln T) ceil(3 ln T)/delta)

source.label: thr:ub_hard
source.quote: Let $\delta\in(0,1)$, $\rho\geq \frac{12K}{T}$, and $\eta= \min\{...\}$ ... Then, \algnamehard suffers a cumulative regret bounded as: $R_T(\lvec_{1:T})\leq {\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}}( \frac{K\ln (\nicefrac{1}{\delta})}{\rho}\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T(\lvec_t^\top(\xvec^\diamond - \xvec^*))^2}+\frac{1}{\rho}\sqrt{K\sum_{t=1}^{T}\lvec_t^\top\xvec^* \ln(\frac{1}{\delta})})$, where $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}$ hides universal constants and logarithmic terms not depending on $\delta$.

results.notes: Statement omits the probability; proof gives w.p. >= 1-5delta and text calls it a high-probability bound. Theorem (thm:safety) separately shows constraints satisfied every round w.p. >= 1-delta (not recorded as a bound). Lemmas (regret:first_part, regret:second_part) are intermediate decomposition bounds, not recorded.

symbols.Delta_c: radius of the constrained small-loss ball: sum_t (l_t^T(x^diamond - x*))^2/T <= Delta_c^2 (not a gap)

conditions: sup over loss sequences in the constrained small-loss ball B_{omega,Delta,T}

source.quote: For all $ \omega \in [0,1]$ and for all $ \Delta \in [0,1]$, it holds $\sup_{\lvec_{1:T} \in \mathcal{B}_{\omega,\Delta, T}} \mathbb{E}[R_T(\lvec_{1:T})] \le \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\frac{K\Delta}{\rho}\sqrt{T}+ \frac{1}{\rho} \sqrt{K\omega T})$, where the expectation is taken with respect to the internal randomization of the algorithm.

results.notes: Algorithm implied to be SOLB (consequence of Theorem thr:ub_hard). Expectation over internal randomization; worst case over the small-loss ball.

symbols.Delta_c: radius of the constrained small-loss ball (squared-distance term), not a gap
symbols.omega: average comparator loss bound of the ball

conditions: sup over loss sequences in B_{omega,Delta,T}
proof considers algorithms that satisfy hard constraints at every round with probability >= 1-delta, delta < 1/2

source.label: thr:lb
source.quote: Let $K\ge 2$, $T \ge \max\{2, (11+\ln T)(\frac{8}{3})^2\}$, and $\omega \in [\frac{1}{T}(\frac{11}{2}+\ln T), \frac{1}{2}]$. Then for every randomized algorithm, we have $\sup_{\lvec_{1:T} \in \mathcal{B}_{\omega,\Delta, T}} \mathbb{E}[R_T(\lvec_{1:T})] \ge \Omega(\frac{\Delta}{\rho}\sqrt{T}+  \sqrt{\omega T})$

results.notes: Statement says 'every randomized algorithm', but the proof uses the safety requirement (hard constraints w.h.p.), hence algorithm_class other. Construction uses K=3 actions with stochastic Bernoulli losses.
